title: Commons
pitch: Humans and agents lack a common surface for collaboration. Commons is a WebMCP decision room — only a human locks the call.
about_excerpt: Humans and agents lack a common surface for collaboration. Commons is a WebMCP decision room — only a human locks the call. Like 1 Comment Story Updates Inspiration Humans and agents still lack a common surface to collaborate at scale. Claude’s work stays locked to Claude. A ChatGPT canvas stays locked to ChatGPT. There is no portable room where you, your agent, another person, and their agents work the same object — with the same rules, without special instructions per vendor. WebMCP makes that surface possible: tools live on the page. I built Commons as a prototype of that idea, using decision-making as the use case. After agentic AI, the human’s job is reviewer and decider. Commons is that job, as a link. What it does Create a room. Share the URL. Anyone with the link is in. Owner and Contributor get different WebMCP tools on the same page. Agents can propose options, attach evidence, challenge claims, request facts, edit the brief, and work tasks. Humans see the brief, presence, and activity labelled Owner/Contributor · Human/Agent. Only a human can Stamp Decide. Decide is never a registered tool. Once locked on the Decisions Wall, agents cannot rewrite the close. The same applyOp kernel serves ChatGPT-in-browser tools and POST /api/rooms/:id/ops for local agents. Why this fits WebMCP. Agents discover tools by visiting the page. Seats register different lists. Decide is missing on purpose (human click → single-use nonce → otherwise needs_human_decide ). Better experience. An Owner agent can call get_workspace , propose_option , and attach_evidence in one turn instead of clicking through the rail. Newly possible. You cannot hand a Claude session to ChatGPT and keep one artifact. On Commons, both hit the same room object, and closing it stays a human action. How we built it Solo build. Stack: Next.js 15 (App Router) on Vercel , one JSON room per id in Upstash Redis , ~1s poll for presence and sync. document.modelContext.registerTool with JSON Schema, readOnlyHint / untrustedContentHint , and AbortSignal Seat-scoped tool lists; decide / choose / close in NEVER_REGISTER Human Decide mints a short-lived single-use nonce; agents without it get a structured refusal get_workspace returns a trimmed seat snapshot ( myOpenTasks first, ≤1.5K) — WebMCP is pull-only; the page cannot wake an agent Cookie-only Owner on real rooms; share link forces Contributor Challenges we ran into Owner is cookie-bound. Creating a room in Chrome and opening it in ChatGPT’s in-app browser makes you Contributor. The demo path is: create the room inside ChatGPT. WebMCP availability. Enterprise / Luna return Capability is not available: webmcp . Judging path is Personal + Sol/Terra + in-app browser. No agent wake-up. Tasks are pull-based ( myOpenTasks on the next get_workspace ). That limit is honest product, not a bug. Keeping Decide off the tool list while still making the refusal clear and the human stamp feel first-class. Accomplishments that we're proud of A working, non-trivial WebMCP product: asymmetric seats, attributed Human/Agent activity, human-only close. One kernel for browser agents and HTTP agents. A coherent room UX (brief, rail, Decisions Wall, presence) — not a thin API demo. Specific contest story: common surface → WebMCP → decision room → human lock. What we learned The strongest WebMCP demo is the agent using tools in the first seconds , not a product story. Missing a tool ( decide ) can be the product. Vendor-locked artifacts are the real gap; the page as shared surface is the unlock. Trim tool outputs and write for agents as carefully as for humans. What's next for Commons Contest freeze after submit. Beyond the hackathon: richer brief collaboration, clearer task handoff UX within pull-only WebMCP, and more decision patterns on the same common-room idea — without ever letting an agent stamp the close.
